headline: Nvidia acquires Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, boosting AI hardware dominance
summary: The AI chip giant is buying the popular open-source AI model repository, often called the "GitHub for AI," in a massive $12.93 billion deal.
details: Nvidia has officially agreed to purchase Hugging Face, a leading platform for open-source AI models, datasets, and tools, for $12.93 billion. This acquisition brings the popular AI community hub under the ownership of the world's largest AI chip manufacturer.

Hugging Face, founded in 2016, functions as a central repository for AI developers to share their projects and data, earning it the nickname "GitHub for AI." Its extensive library of open-source machine learning models and collaborative features make it a vital resource for the AI community.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that the companies will work together to scale Hugging Face's platform, enhance its infrastructure, and broaden access to AI for developers and institutions globally. He assured that Hugging Face will remain an open platform, allowing developers to choose their preferred models, frameworks, and cloud providers, without requiring Nvidia compute.

Speculation about the acquisition began in late August, with reports suggesting Hugging Face was exploring a sale valued around $13 billion. Business Insider and The Information reported on Nvidia's acquisition talks and an impending deal, which Nvidia has now confirmed.

This strategic move by Nvidia aims to solidify its position in the AI hardware market, especially as closed-source AI providers like OpenAI and Google develop their own custom chips. By integrating Hugging Face, Nvidia gains a significant foothold in the open-source AI ecosystem.

Hugging Face was last valued at $4.5 billion in 2023, after a funding round in which Nvidia participated. Previously, the company reportedly rejected a $500 million investment from Nvidia that would have valued it at $7 billion, citing concerns about a dominant single investor.

Despite its strategic importance, Hugging Face's revenue is modest, reportedly around $150 million annually, a fraction of its acquisition price. However, Nvidia's substantial financial resources enable such strategic investments to maintain its AI empire.

headline_marked: Nvidia RTX Spark powers [[first AI PCs]] with up to 6,144 GPU cores
headline: Nvidia RTX Spark powers first AI PCs with up to 6,144 GPU cores
summary: Lenovo's Yoga 9n laptop showcases Nvidia's new Arm-based superchip, aiming for MacBook Pro-level performance and efficiency for on-device AI tasks.
details: Nvidia has officially unveiled its RTX Spark 'superchip,' designed to bring powerful AI capabilities directly to personal computers. The first wave of laptops and mini PCs featuring this chip are now hitting the market, promising enhanced performance for local AI workflows.

The Lenovo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 laptop, a 16-inch device with a premium build and a high-resolution OLED display, is among the first to feature the RTX Spark. Its design rivals the MacBook Pro in thickness and aesthetics, housing an Arm-based SoC that combines a Grace CPU with up to 20 cores and a Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 cores.

This integrated system-on-a-chip (SoC) architecture, similar to Apple's silicon, is expected to offer significant power efficiency, potentially leading to better battery life. Theoretical GPU performance, based on core counts, places it between the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 found in current laptops.

Beyond the 16-inch Yoga 9n, Lenovo also offers a 15-inch Yoga Pro 9n model, which boasts up to 128 GB of memory compared to the 9n's 64 GB limit. Other manufacturers like Dell, Asus, and Microsoft are also preparing to launch their own RTX Spark-powered laptops this fall.

The primary goal of these new AI PCs is to enable users to run complex AI models and agentic workflows locally, reducing reliance on cloud computing. This is particularly important for handling sensitive personal data securely, as AI models can process information without sending it off-device.

In the mini PC space, Acer and Asus are introducing RTX Spark-based solutions that rival the Mac Mini in size but offer substantial AI performance. These devices, alongside AMD-powered alternatives from Lenovo, are poised to play a significant role in the growing adoption of local AI processing.
